MinInitialHp.rationale: BattleFriendV3.cs:15 `MinInitialHp => 300`, a bare literal with no ascension branch. This is one of the seven units SHARED-FINDINGS section 0 lists as INCONCLUSIVE for the `hp` sweep (the roster mis-resolves the shared base); settled by hand here.

SetupSkins.rationale: BattleFriendV3.cs:19-24 selects the spine skin "v3". Presentation (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4).

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's shared verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (battle_friend.py:25-29, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower, 3)`). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40 and relics/paels_legion.py:36-43, and all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, which a self-applied cardless starting power cannot satisfy; (b) HP-roll inversion -- only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581); (c) roll ordering -- `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op. Rule 7: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic/potion/power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Escalation check per SHARED-FINDINGS section 2: self-applied, reads nothing from hooks.combat -- shared verdict fits. Note the applier is NULL on BOTH sides here (BattleFriendV3.cs:35 passes null; battle_friend.py:29 omits it), so this is the one unit family in the batch with no applier divergence. **CORRECTION TO A TOOL, REPORTED NOT FIXED:** `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py ctor-order` flags `__battle_friend` as 'C# model has NO AfterAddedToRoom override'. That is an artifact of the roster mis-resolution (SHARED-FINDINGS section 5) -- the probe resolves `__battle_friend` to a nonexistent BattleFriend.cs and therefore finds no overrides at all. All three real C# files DO override AfterAddedToRoom, at BattleFriendV1.cs:33-36, BattleFriendV2.cs:33-36 and BattleFriendV3.cs:33-36, each applying BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower 3m. Section 2's shared verdict therefore applies unchanged and no escalation is needed.

GenerateMoveStateMachine (protected; add.rationale: Node-by-node against BattleFriendV3.cs:26-31. ONE MoveState, `MoveState("NOTHING_MOVE", _ => Task.CompletedTask)` -- an empty delegate and no intents -- whose FollowUpState is itself, registered as the single-element list and used as the initial state. The sim's shared base builds exactly that (battle_friend.py:31-36: `nothing.follow_up = nothing`, `MonsterMoveStateMachine([nothing], nothing)`, perform delegate `lambda ctx: None`). The dummy never acts on either side; the fight is a timer. No branch state on either side (EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py branch-args`).

guards.what: NOTHING_MOVE carries no intents in C#
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 28.) 'No intent' is now expressible: monsters/base.py gained MoveType.NONE and Intent.none(); all 4 Battle Friend dummy sites construct it, mirroring the empty `params AbstractIntent[]` in BattleFriendV1/V2/V3.cs:28. No consumer tests MoveType.NONE (full_env.py's ten flag checks exclude it, so the dummies encode all-zero flags; test/run.py renders 'None' safely); every other monster's constructed intents are byte-identical (defaulted fields only, verified by a 321-site grep). MoveType.UNKNOWN stays reserved for state_machine.py's UNSET_MOVE sentinel. Witness: test/test_monster_tier_families.py::TestNoIntentUnrepresentable.  The text it replaced read: BattleFriendV3.cs:28 constructs the MoveState with NO intents at all -- the `AbstractIntent[] intents` params array is empty, so the dummy telegraphs nothing. The sim substitutes `Intent(MoveType.UNKNOWN)` (battle_friend.py:32-34). Same mechanism as the StatusIntent-count loss on the_insatiable and aeonglass: the sim's Intent (monsters/base.py:36-59) collapses a C# AbstractIntent[] and cannot express 'no intent'. monster_state_machine's scope boundary item 2 records the whole mapping as audited by no seam. NOT LIVE: nothing in the sim distinguishes UNKNOWN from absent (there is no empty Intent), so no ported consumer can observe it. Named trigger: an observation or replay consumer that renders the intent list, or any content gating on `MonsterModel.IntendsToAttack` (MonsterModel.cs:241-245), which reads the intent list and has no sim counterpart.
